cause_plain: Building a URL fails if one of the URL values is named "self". The call crashes with a TypeError instead of treating "self" as an ordinary value or query parameter.
real_cause: Flask.url_for() declared self as an ordinary parameter, so a URL value named 'self' passed via **values collided with it; the fix makes self positional-only.

cause_plain: A web address that looks malformed (it ends up as "//v:h") made the request crash with a raw urllib3 parsing error. It should have been reported as an invalid URL.
real_cause: HTTPAdapter.request_url() passed a path starting with '//' through unchanged, and urllib3 then parsed '//v:h' as a network location and failed; the fix collapses the leading slashes.

cause_plain: A template failed to render because it tried to join a list of numbers as if they were text. Users got an error instead of the rendered output. I couldn't confirm from the code which template does this.
real_cause: BlockReference.__call__/_async_call joined block output with the module-level str concat instead of environment.concat, so NativeEnvironment blocks returning non-strings failed.

cause_plain: A POST request that got a redirect (like a 302) was resent as a GET with no body. It still claimed it had a body, so the request library refused to send it. The call then failed with a confusing timeout/protocol error.
real_cause: RedirectMiddleware.redirect_headers() kept Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding when a redirect switched the method to GET and dropped the body, so h11 saw too little data for the declared length.

cause_plain: The app crashes on startup, so no one can reach it. One endpoint is set to answer with "204 No Content" but also declares a return type, and FastAPI treats that return type as a response body. FastAPI refuses to build a route that has both.
real_cause: get_typed_annotation() turned the string annotation 'None' (from postponed annotations) into NoneType rather than None, so the route was treated as having a response body and the 204 assertion failed.

cause_plain: Black reformatted a piece of code and the result was not valid Python. Its built-in safety check caught this and refused to output it. The error doesn't include the input, so I can't tell which code triggered it.
real_cause: left_hand_split() only checked for a missing opening bracket, not for empty tail leaves, so at line length 1 it produced a split that broke the code and failed the equivalence check.

cause_plain: Loading data with `sentinel` set to null was rejected because the field doesn't accept null. The library is working as designed here. I can't see the schema that was loaded, so I can't confirm the field was meant to accept null.
real_cause: fields.Constant set load_default/dump_default after Field.__init__ had already computed allow_none from a missing default, so a None constant was rejected as null on load.

cause_plain: Black crashed while formatting a file that contains a multiline (triple-quoted) string. While checking whether a line was short enough, it hit a piece of code that had never been given its nesting depth. It stopped with an internal error instead of formatting the file.
real_cause: blib2to3 Leaf declared bracket_depth only as an annotation and neither __init__ nor clone() set it, so leaves created outside the bracket tracker lacked the attribute that is_line_short_enough() reads.

cause_plain: A class that uses `@define` with a `__attrs_pre_init__` method that takes arguments, and has keyword-only fields with defaults, crashes when it is defined. The generated `__init__` code is malformed, so Python raises a SyntaxError at import time.
real_cause: _attrs_to_init_script() built the __attrs_pre_init__ call from kw_only argument strings that still included '=default', generating invalid code like a=attr_dict['a'].default=a=....

cause_plain: A background cleanup step crashed when a task result object was discarded. The cleanup tries to unsubscribe from the Redis channel for that result. It failed while building the channel name. I can't tell why from what I was shown, so I'm not proposing a fix.
real_cause: BaseKeyValueStoreBackend._get_key_for() passed the task id straight to key_t(), so a uuid.UUID task id made the bytes join raise TypeError.
